mainEntity.name: Do I manage my WPSs in the app or in Excel?

acceptedAnswer.text: In the app. The library is where you work — every WPS, pWPS and WPQR is a structured record you search, filter, edit, verify and link in place. Excel export is there for when a register needs to be handed to your auditors or head office, not something you drop into to get your work done.

mainEntity.name: Can I filter my WPSs by welding process?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Because every field is extracted at import, you filter the library by real criteria — process, base and filler material, position, thickness range and more — down to a specific combination of processes, with or without a backing pass, in a couple of clicks.

mainEntity.name: Can I search on the individual passes?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Facets read the pass table itself, so you can filter on the values inside the passes — side, role, process, polarity — as set-membership filters. Every WPS that runs a 121 root is one click, not a manual read of each document.

Several revisions of the same WPS number collapse into a single row with an N-revisions chip and a switcher, newest first. Each incoming file is classified on import as a new WPS, a new revision, or a correction — so revisions group correctly and the list stays readable.

mainEntity.name: Can I correct a parsed field?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, in place. Edit any field's value or its label and save; a label change re-titles that column in the register, and a one-click verify clears a low-confidence flag. Every correction stays in sync across the library, the register titles and the review badge.

mainEntity.name: Can I link a WPS to its qualification records?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Link a WPS to the WPQR that qualifies it, a WPQR to the several WPS it supports, and a pWPS to the number it becomes — then open any of them in a click and see the whole chain together.
